### Known gaps

- Storage RP account state (StorageProvider.accounts) does not survive a snapshot/restore cycle -- only InMemoryBackend's resource-group/generic-resource/provider-registration state is persisted (see ops.StorageAccountCRUD). Fix is additive: give StorageProvider its own Snapshot/Restore and wire it into Handler.Snapshot/Restore alongside the backend's.
- ServiceBus RP state (ServiceBusProvider's namespaces/queues/topics/subscriptions maps) does not survive a snapshot/restore cycle either, the same known gap as StorageAccountCRUD above and for the same reason -- no ResourceProvider's own state is currently wired into Handler.Snapshot/Restore.
- TestTerraform_Azure_ServiceBus (M9) could not be confirmed against a live tofu apply on this milestone's local macOS development sandbox, due to the same pre-existing host-OS-specific TLS-trust gap documented for M7/M8 (AZURE.md section 10.10) -- apply fails at ARM's own metadata-discovery call, before reaching any ServiceBus-specific code. Compensating verification: test/integration/azurearm_test.go's TestIntegration_AzureARM_ServiceBusLifecycleAndCrossServiceWiring exercises the identical ARM CRUD + cross-service-wiring path over plain HTTP and passed; wire-shape questions were answered by reading the pinned terraform-provider-azurerm/go-azure-sdk source directly. Should be re-confirmed against a green CI run (expected to work on Linux).
- Token endpoint accepts any (or a missing) client_id/grant_type without validation and always issues a token; a malformed client_credentials request should arguably 400 with invalid_request/unsupported_grant_type per RFC 6749, matching AAD's own error shape more closely.
- Direct-data-plane storage resources (azurerm_storage_container/_blob/_queue/_table) are covered as of M8 via the new services/azurestoragevhost virtual-hosted-style listener (AZURE.md section 10.8 finding (9)); azurerm_storage_share (File Share) remains out of scope -- no gopherstack file-share service exists.
- Multi-account namespace isolation: all ARM-created storage accounts alias one shared Blob/Queue/Table container/queue/table namespace (services/azureblob/azurequeue/azuretable discard the account-name path segment entirely). Two ARM storage accounts see each other's containers. Deferred to M10 per AZURE.md section 10.4's original note; StorageAccounts.RegisterAccount/DeleteAccount (interfaces.go) is the forward-compat seam for that fix.
- ARM error codes are a small hand-picked table (errors.go's errorDetails), not audited against ARM's full published error-code catalog the way services/sqs's errorDetails table has been over multiple audit passes.
- management locks, Azure Policy, RBAC/Microsoft.Authorization, ARM template deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments), PATCH-merge semantics beyond full-replace, $filter/$expand and nextLink pagination on list operations, cross-subscription/cross-tenant, resource moves, What-If, and LRO polling are all explicitly out of MVP scope per AZURE.md section 10.1/10.3 -- not bugs, deliberate scope boundaries for this milestone.
- Microsoft.Search: network security perimeter configurations are not modelled (Microsoft.Network networkSecurityPerimeters is not a modelled type, so a perimeter cannot be created to associate a service with).
- Flexible servers: not routed (generic store or 404): migrations (MySQL cutoverMigration) and PostgreSQL virtual-network subnet usage, maintenances (platform-scheduled, nothing in the emulator creates one), logFiles (the engine exposes no log files), backupAndExport (no storage export target), advanced threat protection, detachVNet, resetGtid (no GTID state) and private endpoint connections. Entra administrators (PostgreSQL administrators/{objectId}, MySQL administrators/ActiveDirectory) and the MySQL forced failover are modelled, but the objectId is not resolved against services/azuregraph.
- Flexible servers: replicas and point-in-time/geo restores are state-level (a copy of the source configuration and database list); under the docker engine they are refused with 400 InvalidParameterValue because a new container would start without the source data or the administrator password. Replication is not run.
- Flexible servers: server parameter changes are stored, validated against a documented subset of parameters and flagged pending-restart, but are not applied to the docker engine; max_connections defaults follow the documented per-SKU tables for both engines, but the docker engine itself is not started with that value; the PostgreSQL max_connections range, every other parameter default/range/allowed value, and the MySQL storage IOPS formula (360 minimum, 3 per GiB) are not taken from a published table.
- Flexible servers: firewall rules (including the 0.0.0.0 allow-Azure-services rule) are stored and validated but not enforced - the docker engine listens on loopback only; engines are not relaunched after a gopherstack restart or snapshot restore; the automatic restart of a stopped server (7 days for PostgreSQL, 30 days for MySQL per the Learn how-to pages), maintenance windows, HA failover, data encryption and Entra authentication are stored but not acted on.
- Flexible servers: not modelled although documented - PostgreSQL Premium SSD v2 (storage up to 64 TiB in 1 GiB steps, terraform storage_type PremiumV2_LRS), PostgreSQL confidential-compute SKUs (terraform regex Standard_*C*ads_v5), PostgreSQL E6ds_v4, the PostgreSQL rule that a private DNS zone name must differ from the server name, MySQL storage IOPS pre-provisioning limits below the SKU maximum, and MySQL B1s IOPS (not published).
- AKS: machines (node pools are metadata, so a machine's resource id, IP addresses and name would be fabricated), private endpoint connections (a private endpoint cannot target a managed cluster because the private FQDN and DNS record layout of the API server is not published), managedNamespaces, identityBindings and rotateServiceAccountSigningKeys are not modelled (the generic store keeps what is PUT); node pool snapshots (Microsoft.ContainerService/snapshots) are modelled, but an agent pool cannot yet be created from one, and managedClusterSnapshots have no client in armcontainerservice v9.7.0 and stay in the generic store.
- AKS: node pools are metadata; no VMs back them and the k3s engine runs one server node regardless of pool counts.
- Container Apps: subPath mounts, NfsAzureFile volumes, additional TCP ports, exposedPort/TCP transport routing, session affinity and probes are stored but not run or enforced (the replicas run in the Container Instances engine and ingress is served on the ARM listener, so these are buildable); init containers run before the app containers and ingress ipSecurityRestrictions and corsPolicy are enforced; custom domains, the Dapr runtime and managed-identity registry pulls are stored but need DNS, a Dapr sidecar and an identity token endpoint the emulator does not have.
- Container Apps: only the azure-servicebus and azure-queue (and azureQueue) KEDA scalers read in-process queues; cpu, memory, eventhubs, kafka, redis and other custom scalers are stored but never scale replicas (services/azureeventhubs and services/azureredis exist but are not read by the scaler). Scale-in relies on the pool idle timer (cooldownPeriod) rather than the 300 s scale-down stabilisation window.
- Container Apps: getAuthtoken, listCustomHostNameAnalysis (its customDomainVerificationTest needs a real DNS lookup of the hostname) and diagnostics are not modelled (the generic store keeps what is PUT); authConfigs, sourcecontrols (no GitHub workflow is written), sessionPools (no sessions run), daprComponents, certificates and javaComponents are modelled but components, sessions and authentication run nothing, and the Key Vault certificate source is stored without being fetched.
- Container Instances: exec and attach answer a websocket URI and password and relay through the container runtime (exec runs one command through /bin/sh -c and streams its output; attach sends the current log and closes), but standard input is not relayed, terminalSize is ignored and the socket is served on the ARM listener rather than a regional host.
- Container Instances: not supported and rejected with 400 InvalidRequestContent: confidential/dedicated SKUs, spot priority, encryption, extensions, UDP ports, init container securityContext.
- Container Instances: azureFile volumes are copied from the Azure Files share when the containers start and written back when a container exits and when the group stops or is deleted, not synchronized live; the storage account key is accepted without being checked.
- Container Instances: the group address is 127.0.0.1 and ports are published on pool-assigned host ports (reported in a PortPublished event), not on the declared port numbers; Private addresses behave the same.
- Container Instances: resource requests are validated but only limits are enforced, and per-group CPU/memory maxima are not checked.
- Container Instances: the operations list and container group profiles (Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroupProfiles) are not implemented; a restored snapshot brings groups back Stopped.
- Network: VPN gateways, local network gateways, connections and ExpressRoute circuits with peerings and authorizations are modelled as control-plane resources (no tunnel or circuit state beyond Unknown/NotProvisioned); ExpressRoute ports, links, cross-connections, gateway connections of virtual WAN, VPN sites, point-to-site configuration and every other Microsoft.Network type not listed as modelled stay in the generic metadata-only store (Network Watcher children other than flow logs, such as packet captures and connection monitors, included). DDoS protection plans, private link services, route filters and rules, service endpoint policies and definitions, network watchers with flow logs and virtual network taps are modelled but no protection, mirroring, flow capture or private link traffic runs; the query/set flow log status operations are not modelled; private link service visibility is not enforced on private endpoint creation.
- Application gateways: not modelled - backendSettingsCollection/listeners/routingRules (TCP/TLS proxy), loadDistributionPolicies, entraJWTValidationConfigs, privateLinkConfigurations and privateEndpointConnections (refused with 400), backendHealthOnDemand, available WAF rule sets/SSL options/server variables listings, per-child GET (the armnetwork clients expose none), subnet size sizing (a /24 is recommended, not enforced), NSG and route table requirements of the gateway subnet, Key Vault certificate fetch (keyVaultSecretId is stored, not resolved), user-assigned identity existence, and traffic: no listener serves requests, so request routing, WAF rules, rewrites and redirects are never executed. backendhealth probes only loopback IP backends.
- Azure Firewalls: not modelled - AZFW_Hub / virtualHub firewalls (refused with 400), hubIPAddresses, the read-only ipGroups changeNumber list, packet capture, learned prefixes, DNAT/network/application traffic enforcement, threat intel allowlists enforcement, SNAT private ranges, DNS proxy, Premium TLS inspection/IDPS signatures/overrides, firewall policy drafts and deployments, the FQDN tags listing, the same-resource-group rule for firewall and virtual network, the Basic policy/firewall rule limits, and the maximum counts of rules, IP groups per firewall and addresses per IP group.
- Network: load balancing is control plane only (no traffic distribution, probe execution, SNAT or health state); Basic SKU availability set / same-virtual-network membership rules, Gateway SKU tunnel interfaces and chaining, cross-region (Global tier) backend rules, frontend zones against public IP zones, NAT gateway zone and StandardV2 SKU (rejected), NAT gateway versus Basic public IP or Basic load balancer conflicts, IPv6 load balancer frontends and the privateEndpointNetworkPolicies NSG/UDR behaviour are not modelled or enforced.
- Network: private endpoints ignore cross-subscription authorization (a target in another subscription yields Pending), support static addresses only through ipConfigurations with groupId/memberName matching the group id, write A records for every customDnsConfig FQDN into every zone of a zone group without matching the zone name, allow more than one zone group per endpoint, do not turn a connection Disconnected when its target is deleted, and omit the Event Grid, Cosmos mongoClusters, Application Gateway, Private Link service and other private-link target types.
- Network: IPv6 private addresses on NICs are rejected; IPv6 public addresses come from 2001:db8::/32. Subnet addressing with ipamPoolPrefixAllocations and NAT/gateway-subnet rules are not enforced (NICs report the virtualMachine and primary back-references of an attached Compute VM but never hostedWorkloads).
- Private DNS: auto-registration of NIC addresses into linked zones, one-registration-link-per-vnet and overlapping-namespace conflicts and Microsoft.Network/dnszones (public DNS) are not implemented.
- Compute: shared and community galleries stay in the generic metadata-only store; not modelled on placement resources: dedicated host redeploy, hostSizes, capacity reservation sharing across subscriptions and block schedules, disk access private endpoint connections, Key Vault key existence for encryption sets and disk encryption set rotation.
- Compute: virtual machines do not run; unmanaged (vhd) disks, inline networkInterfaceConfigurations, boot diagnostics, maintenance, capture (needs unmanaged VHD blobs, which are rejected) and convertToManagedDisks answer 501 NotImplemented or are rejected.
- Compute: disks accept Empty, FromImage, Copy and Upload; Import, ImportSecure, Restore and CopyStart are rejected, beginGetAccess/endGetAccess answer 501 (an Upload disk stays ReadyToUpload), and Ultra/Premium v2 IOPS limits, shared disks (maxShares), bursting, encryption sets and zone-versus-VM zone matching are stored but not enforced.
- Compute: Uniform scale set instances are state records, so their network interfaces are not created in Microsoft.Network and subnets referenced by a Uniform scale set can still be deleted. Rolling upgrades, autoscale, scale-in policy (Flexible removes the newest machines first), Uniform per-instance power actions and instance-level PUT/PATCH are not implemented.
- Compute: a virtual machine cannot be added to an availability set after creation (PropertyChangeNotAllowed) and an omitted availabilitySet, osProfile or storageProfile on update keeps the stored value.
- ManagedIdentity: assignmentRestrictions and the api-versions 2025-01-31-preview and 2025-05-31-preview are not implemented; isolationScope is stored and echoed but never enforced; listAssociatedResources scans Compute, Web, Container Instances, Container Apps and AKS resources only; resource group deletion removes same-named groups of identities in every subscription.
- API Management: not modelled - the built-in all-access (master) subscription, the starter/unlimited products and built-in groups, diagnostics, certificates, gateways (self-hosted), portal, schemas, API revisions/releases, product groups and group users, user subscriptions, wikis, issues, tenant settings, backup/restore, soft-delete/restore, custom hostnames, virtual networks, multi-region, private endpoints, v2 tiers (BasicV2, StandardV2) and the Isolated sku; they fall to 404 or are rejected. $top, $skip, count and nextLink paging work on the child lists; $filter is not implemented.
- API Management gateway: policies outside the subset (validate-jwt, quota, ip-filter, cache, choose, set-variable, send-request, authentication-*, policy expressions, product-scope policies, on-error execution, rate-limit nested api/operation, forward-request http-version/continue-timeout/buffer-*/fail-on-error-status-code, cors terminate-unmatched-request) are refused at PUT or not honoured; the backend section runs set-header/set-query-parameter/set-backend-service/forward-request in order and a chain with no forward-request answers an empty 200. The cors policy page gives two defaults for terminate-unmatched-request (false in the attribute table, true in the usage notes), so unmatched simple requests proceed without CORS headers. set-header on Connection, Content-Length, Keep-Alive and Transfer-Encoding is accepted but those headers are never forwarded (Learn: they cannot be changed).
- API Management gateway: WebSocket and GraphQL APIs are served as plain HTTP passthrough (ws/wss serviceUrl answers 500); HTTP (non-TLS) calls are impossible because the ARM listener is HTTPS, so an API whose protocols exclude https answers 404; the gateway has no client-certificate, IP or JWT checks; failed upstream calls answer 502 where the real gateway answers 500 (unverified); the unknown-host 404 body Resource not found and the 503 body of a service that is still activating are gopherstack wording, not documented.
- Authorization: with --azure-arm-enforce-rbac, ARM requests under a resource group are evaluated against the bearer token's role assignments (action derived as {namespace}/{type}/{read|write|delete|action}); data planes, subscription-level and management-group requests are not evaluated; there is no deny-assignment API because only Blueprints, managed applications and similar services create deny assignments and none is emulated, so evaluation has no deny source; no PIM/eligibility/schedule, classic administrator or provider-operations API, no management-group scope for locks, and management group scopes are accepted but never checked to exist; managed-identity token endpoints do not exist, so a system-assigned identity cannot obtain a token to be evaluated.
- Authorization: ScopeLocked enforcement covers the ARM listener only (not data planes, as documented); it does not model the documented exceptions where services act on locked resources, resource moves, or Microsoft.Authorization extension resources other than the lock itself inheriting a lock (role assignments and policy assignments do inherit it).
- Authorization: role assignment conditions (ABAC) are stored and validated (conditionVersion 2.0, balanced brackets) but never evaluated, because evaluation needs the request attributes of the data plane that carries the attribute namespaces; delegatedManagedIdentityResourceId is stored; the last-owner deletion guard does not exist; assignableScopes of management groups are not checked to exist; list calls are not paged (no nextLink/$skipToken).
- Policy: deny, audit, append and modify are evaluated at write time (PUT of a resource group or resource) for rules that read type, name, id, location, kind and tags with parameters(), concat() and field(); rules that read aliases, requestContext() or resourceGroup() are skipped, as are auditIfNotExists, deployIfNotExists and denyAction, so no remediation, policy versions, tokens or allowed-locations deny on aliased types exist; compliance states are recorded per resource and definition and persisted, but there is no Microsoft.PolicyInsights read API because armpolicyinsights is not in the module cache; exemptions are honoured; policyDefinitions is limited to a 13-definition and 1-initiative built-in catalog; initiative parameters are not checked against their member definitions; the Guest Configuration provider does not exist.
- Authorization: management-group scoped policy assignments have no Terraform fixture (azurerm_management_group needs a tenant-level group API the emulator does not model); azurerm_role_definition, subscription policy assignments and policy set definitions are applied, planned clean and destroyed by TestTerraform_Azure_AuthorizationScoped, and test/terraform/azure/flexible_test.go and apim_test.go cover the Flexible Server and API Management resources named there.
- Logic: not routed (answer 404 NotFound): workflows move, generateUpgradedDefinition and listSwagger, run operations, action repetitions, scopeRepetitions, requestHistories and listExpressionTraces, and every Integration Account and Integration Service Environment API.
- Logic: only Request and Recurrence triggers fire. Http polling, HttpWebhook, Workflow and SlidingWindow triggers are stored but never run.
- Logic expression functions: date formatting and parsing know the en-US, fr-FR and es-ES names only; other locales are rejected.
- Logic: trigger concurrency (runtimeConfiguration.concurrency.runs, SingleInstance) and maximumWaitingRuns are not honoured; runtimeConfiguration.secureData and staticResult are ignored.
- Logic: the Http action does not follow the 202 asynchronous Location pattern and supports Basic and Raw authentication only (no ActiveDirectoryOAuth, ClientCertificate or ManagedServiceIdentity); cookies are not sent.
- Logic: actions inside Foreach and Until are recorded as one aggregated action (status and times) in run history; per-iteration records, inputs and outputs are not exposed because the repetitions APIs are not routed.

### Deferred

- M7 initial implementation. No prior audit passes to report.
- M9 added the Microsoft.ServiceBus RP (ServiceBusNamespaceCRUD/ServiceBusQueueTopicSubscriptionCRUD/ServiceBusAuthorizationRuleListKeys). QC pass over the pre-existing implementation found and fixed two real bugs before any Terraform run (List not filtering by resource group for queues/topics/subscriptions; DeleteResourcesInGroup's cascade delete never matching due to a double-pipe key-prefix bug) -- see AZURE.md section 10.10's M9 entry for full detail.
- M9's first real-CI run (PR #2466, terraform-tests (6) job on Linux, past the macOS TLS-trust gap) surfaced a third real bug: classifyServiceBusPath had no case for namespaces/{ns}/networkRuleSets/default, which terraform-provider-azurerm's namespace Read calls unconditionally on every namespace regardless of SKU or config -- see ops.ServiceBusNamespaceNetworkRuleSet above and AZURE.md section 10.10's M9 entry for full detail. Checked queue/topic/subscription/authorizationRule Read functions in the same pinned source for the same class of unconditional sub-resource probe; none exists (each Read function only calls its own client.Get).
